title: Quantized-model fallback orchestrator and canary safety-net for calibration drift
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight orchestrator that drives canary rollouts for quantized model variants (FP8/INT8) and automatically falls back to a safe serving variant when calibration or accuracy checks fail. This ticket focuses on the safety-net logic, decision thresholds, and the calibration drift detector that gates canary promotion. We will not change kernel-level quantization code in this ticket; instead we integrate profiling, validation, and routing policies into the serving control plane.

Motivation: Customers running quantized variants sometimes see silent accuracy regressions after model/weights refreshes, prompt drift, or data distribution shifts. We need an automated safety net so production traffic is preserved while still allowing controlled experimentation with aggressive quantization profiles.

Non-goals: Implementing new quantization transforms, changing training pipelines, or adding model-specific calibration tooling beyond sample collection and metric evaluation. Those are tracked in ENG-45150 and ENG-45560.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Canary stage can be launched for a quantized variant and routed only 1-5% of traffic using existing routing policies.
A2: Calibration drift detector runs on canary samples and computes pass/fail within 60s of sample window close using the golden prompt suite.

A3: If any configured quality gate (accuracy delta, perplexity, BLEU-like metric) exceeds threshold, routing shifts back to baseline variant automatically within the configured adaptation window and an incident record is created.
A4: The orchestrator records decision metadata (metric snapshot, sample summary, reason) to the rollout audit log and exposes it to Console and tracing endpoints.
A5: Automated smoke tests simulate a failure mode and assert that fallback completes and that SLA (p95 latency) remains within tolerance during the switchover.
A6: Dashboard panels show canary pass rate, rollback events, and drift score time series for a 30-day window.
A7: No customer data is sent to external services; sample aggregation respects privacy and KMS rules already enforced by runtime-1.20.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Add a lightweight Canary Orchestrator microcomponent in control plane that subscribes to rollout requests and evaluation results.

Step 2: Integrate calibration drift detector that compares canary outputs against golden prompt suite and baseline outputs using configurable metrics (delta-accuracy, response-embedding-cosine, token-level KL).

Step 3: Implement policy engine rules: fail gates, soft-throttle (reduce traffic), hard-fallback (switch routing to baseline), and alert generation. Policies are parameterized per-model and per-profile.
Step 4: Wire decision logging to rollout-audit index and expose events via Console API /internal/rollouts/{id}/events.
Step 5: Add end-to-end tests: synthetic sample injection, simulated distribution shift, and latency smoke tests. Ensure tests run in CI with mocked runtime connectors.
Step 6: Ship feature flag behind runtime.canary_fallback_v1 and enable on a small set of experiments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): Unit + integration tests in CI, local emulation using small Llama config. Owner: Diego.
Phase 1 (canary): Enable feature flag for internal tenants and run 5 internal canaries with golden suite. Monitor for 48 hours. Owner: SRE + Diego.
Phase 2 (gradual): Expand to beta customers that opt-in via Console UI. Keep traffic cap at 1%. Rollouts automatically revert on fail. Owner: Customer Ops.
Phase 3 (GA): Open to all customers with conservative defaults and docs on tuning gates. Add templates for FP8 and INT8 profiles. Owner: Product + Eng.
Rollback trigger: any hard-fail gate or >0.5% customer-impacting degradation in quality signals over 24h.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: quant.canary.drift_score (lower is better) - alert when > configured threshold for 3 consecutive windows.
Metric: quant.canary.rollback_count - alert on >1 rollback per model per week.
SLOs: p95 latency should not increase >15% during fallback switchover.
Logging: decision payload (model, profile, metric snapshot, sample IDs) stored in rollout-audit for 90 days.
Dashboard: new Console tab 'Quant Canary' with per-model timeline, pass/fail badges and recent audit events.
testing: Unit: policy engine rule evaluation for pass/soft-fail/hard-fail paths.
Integration: end-to-end canary run with mocked runtime emitting drift metric; assert fallback completes and audit event present.
Chaos: introduce latency spike and verify that fallback does not exacerbate p95 beyond tolerance.
Regression: run golden prompt suite (1000 examples stratified by prompt length & domain) and assert error budgets.
decision_log: 2025-11-04: Decided to use a golden prompt suite plus embedding-cosine and token-KL as primary signals after benching on 5 models (Maya/Diego).
2025-11-06: Chose soft-throttle (traffic reduction) as intermediate mitigation before hard fallback to avoid oscillation (SRE review).
2025-11-07: Agreed to keep default thresholds conservative for FP8; INT8 profiles use tighter pass gates.

notes: Implementation should be backward-compatible with existing rollout constructs. Keep policy configuration exposed via Console with sane defaults. Coordinate with Product for messaging and with Support for post-rollout monitoring playbook.
